slides.title: Respiratory System
text: Air movement from higher pressures to lower

slides.title: Pneumonia
text: inflammatory process of lung/parenchyma commonly caused by infectious agents entering via aspiration or inhalation
Pleuritic pain, pleural rub, dyspnea, Tachypnea
Consolidation of lung tissue – white “patchy” infiltrate on CXR
Classified as either bacterial or viral
Elderly may present w/ few s/s

slides.title: Positioned w/ affected lung down
text: Atelectasis:  affected lung would be up, to promote lung expansion of affected side
Encourage client to turn, cough, and deep breath, splint chest wall, use incentive spirometer

slides.title: Pulmonary Tuberculosis
text: A bacterial infectious disease transmitted by Mycobacterium tuberculosis
Primarily affects the lungs but can spread to any organ in the blood
Risk of transmission decreases after 2 to 3 weeks of antitubercular therapy
Will have a positive intradermal TB test within 2 to 10 weeks of exposure to the infection

slides.title: TB Skin Test
text: TB syringe (1 cc, ½ in, 26-27 g needle)
Intradermal, hold needle parallel to skin so hub touches skin, bevel up
Inject solution (0.01mL) and watch for wheal
Circle the site, record date, time, location of injection and type of dose given
Results are read at 48 and 72 hours after the injection

slides.title: PPD only indicates that body developed antibodies against tubercle bacilli
text: PPD only indicates that body developed antibodies against tubercle bacilli
Does not indicate if tubercle bacilli are dormant or growing
If antibodies are present, PPD will be positive
90% of persons w/ +PPD never develop active TB
PPD only the induration is measured (hardened or thick tissue) – not just redness
=/>5 mm – if close contact with active TB, HIV + , recent immigrant
=/>10 mm– health care workers and injection drug users
=/>15 mm– if no risk factors for TB
What if the PPD is positive?

slides.title: TBSputum Specimen Collection
text: Early am, do not brush teeth, rinse mouth w/ water only, no mouthwash or toothpaste
Take several deep breaths and deep cough
Do not let mouth or sputum touch outside of sterile container
Cover immediately and send to lab

slides.title: Pulmonary Tuberculosis
text: TB heals slowly, combination drug therapy more effective
Take drugs regularly, if interrupted, drug resistance will occur
Isoniazid (INH):  most potent TB drug. Bactericidal-given to prevent active TB in converters
Pyrazinamide - (Pyridoxine/B6) – given to prevent nerve damage
Do I need to monitor any labs with theses medications?

slides.title: Pulmonary Tuberculosis
text: Use of private negative pressure room, N95 mask, and airborne precautions
Good ventilation decreases concentration of airborne organism’s
Activity restriction 2 – 4 weeks after treatment started
Cover mouth when coughing or sneezing

slides.title: COPD
text: A broad classification that includes a group of conditions associated with chronic obstruction of airflow entering or leaving lungs

slides.title: Chronic Bronchitis
text: Develops from infections and repeated irritations
Irritants such as cigarette smoke and air pollution
History of habitual cigarette smoking and morning cough
Subjective data – dyspnea, cough, sputum, pain, fever and anorexia
Smoking hx - # packs x # yrs. = pack years

slides.title: Emphysema
text: Causes: late result of chronic bronchial irritation or infection
Increased dead space (no gas exchange occurs)
Accessory muscles to aid work of breathing

slides.title: COPDPursed Lip Breathing
text: Expiration 2 x  as long as inspiration.  Helps empty lungs of trapped air
Breathe in slowly thru nose with mouth closed. This will warm, filter and moisten the air
To breathe out, purse lips, like your whistling, and slowly blow out at least twice as long as you breathed in
DO NOT blow hard enough to puff the checks out

slides.title: COPDChest Physical Therapy (CPT)
text: Postural Drainage – positioning a lung segment so secretions will drain out of the lung by gravity. It can then be coughed up
Percussion – clapping the chest wall over the lung segment to be drained to force secretions loose from the bronchioles
Vibration – using vibrating motions on the chest wall with the open hands to squeeze secretions out of the small airways.  Mechanical vibrators are also available

slides.title: COPDPulmonary Function Tests
text: Breathe into a machine thru the mouth
Will be asked to breathe in different ways, deep breath in and out
Bronchodilators not given prior to test

slides.title: COPDAdrenergic Bronchodilators
text: Actions:  dilates bronchial smooth muscle, increases ciliary movement
Side Effects:  tachycardia, palpitations, HTN, dyspnea, HA, dilated pupils, anxiety, nervousness, GI upset
Inhaled route preferred – less side effects

slides.title: COPDCorticosteroids
text: Actions:  anti-inflammatory, decreases antibody formation, relaxes smooth muscle of bronchial airways
Side Effects:  GI irritation, delayed wound healing, more prone to infection, increased blood sugars, osteoporosis
Nursing Implications:  gradually d/c drug, watch for adrenal insufficiency (may take up to 1 year for adrenal glands to start working again). Administer with food

slides.title: COPDAnticholinergic Agent
text: Causes bronchodilation for acute bronchospasm, decreases bronchial secretions
Good for asthmatics who cannot take beta agonists or xanthenes d/t cardiac problems

slides.title: COPDXanthine Agents
text: Aminophylline – IV (Aminodur), PO (Theodur, Theolair, Theolair SR)
Has direct CNS action to relax smooth muscles (esp bronchial), increases movement of mucus, increases contraction of diaphragm, bronchodilates
Side effects:  anxiety, restlessness, HA, nervousness, insomnia, convulsions, increased heart rate, palpitation, hypotension, decreased urinary output. (N/V, gastric irritation – po route)
Drug level – theophylline level 10-20 mcg/mL,  toxic if >20

slides.title: NGN NCLEX-RN Question
text: The home health nurse is caring for a 26-year-old client who has pulmonary tuberculosis and is receiving newly prescribed streptomycin 1 gram intramuscular (IM) once daily. Which of the following actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.
Remind the client to monitor for hearing changes.
Tell the client to contact the primary health care provider if the stool is black.
Advise the client to take over-the-counter acetaminophen for fever and headache.
Inform the client that there is no need for a follow-up visit once the medication is completed.
Advise the client to continue streptomycin therapy before any procedures that may require anesthesia.
